counters.name: Counter aggregation and bucketing
counters.desc: Period pixels count matching events, bucket the total at period end, and enqueue one pixel per period carrying the bucket name. A pixel whose parameters produce no values does not fire, which is why the zero-bucket cases differ: the captcha pixels have a 0 bucket and fire with count=0, the adwall day pixel has no zero bucket and stays silent. Time-derived parameters such as attributionPeriod are excluded from comparison.

tests.name: Occurrences across pages bucket at period end
tests.desc: Three occurrences on distinct pages count 3, landing in the 3-5 bucket for both the day and week pixels independently.

tests.name: A zero count fires when a zero bucket exists
tests.desc: No matching events arrive. The captcha pixels' 0 bucket matches a zero count, so they fire with count=0; the adwall pixels stay silent.

tests.name: A count matching no bucket does not fire
tests.desc: The adwall day pixel has no zero bucket, so with nothing counted it must not fire. The unrelated event does not count towards it either.

tests.name: A disabled pixel never fires
tests.desc: webTelemetry_disabledPixel_day would fire on any count, but its state is disabled.

immediate.name: Immediate pixels
immediate.desc: Immediate pixels fire once per delivered event with data parameters forwarded from the event payload. The hub de-duplicates web events at ingestion, before fan-out (see the event-hub/deduplication suite), so repeats of an event type on one page fire once - the same single delivery the counter on that stream counts.

tests.name: One immediate pixel per event type per page
tests.desc: Two occurrences on the same page are one delivery: one immediate pixel carrying the first occurrence's payload (the second is dropped at the hub, its payload with it), while the counter on the same event counts the page once.

tests.name: An event with no matching immediate trigger fires nothing immediately
A disabled immediate pixel never fires
tests.desc: webTelemetry_disabledPixel_immediate shares the adwallDetected trigger with the enabled immediate pixel but its state is disabled, so only the enabled one fires. Disabled state gates every trigger type, not only period pixels.
